english.title: Release / market / import / acquire genetically modified organism without risk assessment / notice to Secretary of State
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) contravened section 108(1) of the Environmental Protection Act 1990 in relation to something which was and which you knew or had reason to believe was a genetically modified organism in that you

(A)_[imported]_
(B)_[acquired]_
(C)_[released]_
(D)_[marketed]_

that organism without

(E)_[carrying out an assessment of risk]_
(F)_[giving notice to the Secretary of State of your intention to do so]_

as required
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 108(1) and 118(1)(a) and (5) of the Environmental Protection Act 1990.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 118(2) of the Environmental Protection Act 1990 provides that It shall be a defence for a person charged with an offence under this paragraph to prove that he took all reasonable precautions and exercised all due diligence to avoid the commission of this offence.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Five years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
